topic: Buying New Year decorations at the shrine

guest.name: 宮下さん
guest.name_jp: {宮下正雄|みやしたまさお}さん
guest.role: the elderly priest of {鷹ノ原神社|たかのはらじんじゃ}; slow, old-fashioned polite speech

title_jp: しめ{飾り|かざり}と{一夜飾り|いちやかざり}
context: Wednesday 30 December: with {田中|たなか}さん's back still bad, アルちゃん goes to {鷹ノ原神社|たかのはらじんじゃ} to buy the New Year rope decoration, after picking up rice cakes at the rice shop. The old priest, {宮下|みやした}さん, already knows about the bad back.
scene: Wednesday. {田中|たなか}さん can't lift a thing, so you're at the town shrine to buy the New Year decoration. The old priest already knows why.

phrases.jp: {買い物|かいもの}のついでに、{神社|じんじゃ}に{寄って|よって|to drop in|4}きた。
phrases.en: I stopped by the shrine while I was out shopping.
phrases.note: Noun + のついでに = while doing that anyway.

phrases.jp: {私|わたし}は、いい{習慣|しゅうかん}だと{思います|おもいます}。
phrases.en: I think it's a good custom.
phrases.note: The basic way to give an opinion politely.

phrases.jp: {迷信|めいしん|superstition|2}かもしれないけど、{大切|たいせつ}にしたいな。
phrases.en: It might be a superstition, but I want to respect it.

phrases.jp: それは{縁起|えんぎ|luck, omen|3}が{悪い|わるい}ですよ。
phrases.note: {縁起|えんぎ}がいい = lucky. You'll hear both all through New Year.

phrases.jp: {正直|しょうじき}、どっちでもいいと{思う|おもう}。
phrases.en: Honestly, I don't think it matters either way.
phrases.note: A soft way to say you don't mind.

dialogue_setting: The charm window of {鷹ノ原神社|たかのはらじんじゃ}, Wednesday morning. Snow on the roofs, a bag of rice cakes in your hand.

dialogue.speaker: 宮下さん
dialogue.jp: おや、{田中|たなか}さんとこのスペインの{方|かた}ですな。お{父|とう}さんの{腰|こし}の{具合|ぐあい|condition (of health)|3}はどうです？
dialogue.en: Ah, you're the Spanish gentleman staying with the 田中s. How's his back?
dialogue.note: 〜ですな = old-fashioned 〜ですね. 〜とこ = 〜のところ (the household of).

dialogue.speaker: アルちゃん
dialogue.jp: もうご{存じ|ぞんじ|(honorific) to know|2}なんですか！{米屋|こめや}でお{餅|もち|rice cake|4}を{受け取る|うけとる|to receive, collect|3}ついでに、しめ{飾り|かざり|New Year rope decoration|3}を{買い|かい}に{来ました|きました}。
dialogue.en: You already know! I'm picking up rice cakes at the rice shop, so while I'm at it I came to buy the New Year decoration.

dialogue.speaker: 宮下さん
dialogue.jp: {今日|きょう}{飾る|かざる|to decorate, put up|3}なら{結構|けっこう}。{明日|あした}だと「{一夜飾り|いちやかざり|decorating only the night before|2}」で、{縁起|えんぎ|luck, omen|3}が{悪い|わるい}と{言われとります|いわれとります}。
dialogue.en: If you put it up today, that's fine. Tomorrow would be 'one-night decorating', which is said to bring bad luck.
dialogue.note: 〜とります = 〜ております (older regional speech).

dialogue.speaker: アルちゃん
dialogue.jp: {迷信|めいしん|superstition|2}かもしれませんが、{私|わたし}は{好き|すき}です。{神様|かみさま|god, the gods|4}を{丁寧|ていねい}に{迎える|むかえる}{感じ|かんじ}がして。
dialogue.en: It might be a superstition, but I like it. It feels like welcoming the gods properly.

dialogue.speaker: 宮下さん
dialogue.jp: わしもそう{思います|おもいます}な。{伝統|でんとう|tradition|3}は、{形|かたち}より{心|こころ}が{大事|だいじ|important|4}だと{考えとります|かんがえとります}。
dialogue.en: I think so too. With traditions, I believe the heart matters more than the form.
dialogue.note: わし = an old man's 'I'. Don't copy it.

dialogue.speaker: アルちゃん
dialogue.jp: じゃあ、{一つ|ひとつ}ください。{元日|がんじつ}は{初詣|はつもうで|first shrine visit of the year|3}のついでに、お{守り|まもり|charm, amulet|3}も{買います|かいます}ね！
dialogue.en: Then one, please. On New Year's Day I'll buy a charm too when I come for my first shrine visit!

listening.intro: As you leave, {宮下|みやした}さん calls a reminder after you.

lines.jp: {今日|きょう}のうちに、{玄関|げんかん|entrance (of a house)|3}に{飾って|かざって|to put up|3}くださいな。
lines.en: Put it up on the front door today, won't you.

grammar.form: verb: dictionary or た-form + ついでに ({受|う}け{取|と}るついでに, {行|い}ったついでに) · noun: + のついでに ({買|か}い{物|もの}のついでに, {初詣|はつもうで}のついでに)
grammar.explanation: You're doing A anyway, so you also do B, taking the chance. A is the main errand; B is the extra. Don't swap them: {神社|じんじゃ}に{行|い}くついでに{旅行|りょこう}する sounds odd, because the trip is the big thing.

examples.jp: コンビニに{行く|いく}ついでに、ゴミを{出して|だして}くれる？
examples.en: While you're going to the konbini, could you take the rubbish out?

examples.jp: {散歩|さんぽ}のついでに、ポストに{手紙|てがみ}を{入れた|いれた}。
examples.en: I posted a letter while I was out for a walk.

quiz.question: {駅|えき}に{行く|いく}＿＿、{切符|きっぷ}も{買って|かって}きて。
quiz.en: While you're going to the station, buy the tickets too.
quiz.explain: Verb dictionary form + ついでに, no の.

quiz_more.question: {買い物|かいもの}＿＿ついでに、{郵便局|ゆうびんきょく}に{寄った|よった}。
quiz_more.en: I stopped at the post office while I was shopping.

quiz_more.question: {米屋|こめや}に{行った|いった}＿＿、{神社|じんじゃ}に{寄った|よった}。
quiz_more.en: While I was at the rice shop anyway, I dropped in at the shrine.
quiz_more.explain: Verb (here た-form) + ついでに. の only comes after a noun.

kanji.meaning: the shrine window for charms and talismans
kanji.where: Above the little wooden window where {宮下|みやした}さん sits.
kanji.breakdown: {授与所|じゅよしょ}: 授 give + 与 give, bestow + 所 place → 'the place where things are given'. Shrines avoid the word 'sell'.
kanji.related: お{守|まも}り = charm; お{札|ふだ} = paper talisman for the home.

tip.title: When to put up New Year decorations
tip.body: Many families put up しめ{飾|かざ}り and {門松|かどまつ} around 28 December. The 29th is avoided because 9 (く) sounds like {苦|く}, suffering, and the 31st is 'one-night decorating', thought rude to the New Year god. They come down around 7 January (later in some regions).

challenge.prompt: Back home, {颯太|そうた} on the family LINE: 「アルちゃん、{明日|あした}ハナばあちゃんとそば{打ち|うち|making (noodles) by hand|2}でしょ？{俺|おれ}もやりたい！」 You think that's a great idea. Which sticker?
challenge.explanation: いいね！ is the casual 'great idea!' for a suggestion. ごめん！ would sound like you're saying no, {怖|こわ}い… makes no sense here, and お{疲|つか}れ{様|さま}です is a work greeting, far too stiff for an 11-year-old.

vocab.note: {具合|ぐあい}が{悪|わる}い = feel unwell. Also for machines.
{受|う}ける receive + {取|と}る take. Parcels, orders, change.
{飾|かざ}り = a decoration. しめ{飾|かざ}り, {正月飾|しょうがつかざ}り.
{縁起|えんぎ}がいい / {悪|わる}い = lucky / unlucky. {縁起物|えんぎもの} = lucky charm.
Shinto has countless {神様|かみさま}, so no 'the one God' nuance.
A bit softer than {大切|たいせつ}. お{大事|だいじ}に = get well soon.

vocab.en: first shrine visit of the year
vocab.note: {初|はつ} first + {詣|もうで} pilgrimage. Usually 1–3 January.
From {守|まも}る (protect). One for exams, traffic safety, love…

kanji_study.parts: An old drawing of a cauldron (now like 目) held up by two hands below → hands holding up a vessel: things provided, tools.
kanji_study.lookalike: Not 貝 (shell): 具 has three lines inside and a long flat stroke underneath.

kanji_study.kun: なお(る)・なお(す)・おさ(める)
kanji_study.parts: 氵 water radical + 台 platform → building banks to keep rivers under control: govern; and a body brought back under control: heal.
kanji_study.lookalike: Not 冶 (smelt): 冶 has two ice strokes 冫, 治 has three water strokes 氵.
